verses.text: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the LORD's eyes, as his ancestor David had done.
Instead he followed the ways of the kings of Israel. He even made metal idols of the Baal gods.
He burned incense in the Valley of Ben Hinnom and burned his own sons as sacrifices in the fire. He copied the disgusting practices of the nations the LORD had driven out ahead of the Israelites.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the hilltop shrines, on the hills, and under every green tree.

So the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Syria. The Syrians defeated him and took many of his people as prisoners to Damascus. He was also handed over to the king of Israel, who killed a great many of his men.
In one day Pekah son of Remaliah killed one hundred twenty thousand brave soldiers in Judah, because they had left the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Zichri, a strong warrior from Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the officer in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, the king's second in command.
The Israelites took two hundred thousand of their own relatives from Judah as prisoners: women, sons, and daughters. They also took a lot of loot and brought it to Samaria.

But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army when it came to Samaria and said, "Look, the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, so he handed them over to you. But you have killed them with a rage that reaches up to heaven.
Now you plan to make the people of Judah and Jerusalem your slaves, men and women. But aren't you also guilty of sins against the LORD your God?
Now listen to me! Send back the prisoners you have taken from your relatives, because the LORD's fierce anger is on you."

Then some of the leaders of Ephraim stood up against the men coming back from the war. They were Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.
They said to them, "Do not bring the prisoners here! You want to add to our sin and guilt against the LORD. Our guilt is already great, and his fierce anger is on Israel."
So the soldiers left the prisoners and the loot in front of the leaders and all the people.

The men named above took charge of the prisoners. They used the loot to give clothes to everyone who was naked. They gave them clothes, sandals, food, and drink, and put healing oil on their wounds. They put all the weak ones on donkeys and took them to their relatives in Jericho, the City of Palm Trees. Then they went back to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz asked the kings of Assyria for help.
The Edomites had come again, attacked Judah, and taken prisoners.

The Philistines had also raided the towns in the foothills and in the south of Judah. They captured and settled in Beth Shemesh, Aijalon, and Gederoth, and Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo with their villages.
The LORD brought Judah down because of Ahaz king of Israel, who let Judah run wild and was very unfaithful to the LORD.
Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came to him, but he caused him trouble instead of helping him.
Ahaz took some things from the LORD's temple, from the palace, and from the leaders, and gave them to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.
Even in his time of trouble, King Ahaz was even more unfaithful to the LORD.

He offered sacrifices to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him. He thought, "The gods of the kings of Syria helped them, so I will offer sacrifices to them so they will help me." But they caused his ruin and the ruin of all Israel.
Ahaz gathered the things from God's temple and cut them into pieces. He shut the doors of the LORD's temple and set up altars on every street corner in Jerusalem.
In every town in Judah he built hilltop shrines to burn incense to other gods. This made the LORD, the God of his ancestors, angry.
Everything else he did and all his ways, from beginning to end, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz died and was buried in the city of Jerusalem, but not in the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah became king after him.
